title: Standardized procedures for thoracentesis / pleural biopsy at Pleural Diseases Outpatient Clinic - HUPE / UERJ
author: Ana Paula Santos

steps_raw.instruction: Standardized procedures for thoracentesis / pleural biopsy at Pleural Diseases Outpatient Clinic - HUPE / UERJ
Ana Paula Santos1, Thiago Mafort1, Rogério Rufino1
1 Department of Pulmonary Care, Pedro Ernesto University Hospital (HUPE) - State University of Rio de Janeiro (UERJ), RJ/Brazil.
This document is intended for the standardization of stepwise procedures to perform thoracentesis and pleural biopsy at HUPE / UERJ.
General considerations:

Patients are referred to the Pleural Disease Outpatient Clinic of HUPE / UERJ at the hospital's own request or by reference of the Health System of Rio de Janeiro State for thoracentesis and pleural biopsy.
The following materials are required:
- Chlorhexidine and gauze for skin antisepsis;
- Conventional peripheral intravenous catheter;
- Syringes (5 mL and 20 mL) and needles;
- Lidocaine without vasoconstrictor;
- Collection tubes and disposable jars.
Phase 1. Clinical interview before the procedure:

During the medical interview before the procedure, which is held at Pulmonary Department at HUPE / UERJ once a week, anamnesis and physical examination are performed. The blood tests required for the procedure (blood count, coagulogram, blood glucose, amylase, triglycerides, total proteins and fractions, total bilirubin and fractions, DHL) and chest radiographs are analysed by the medical doctor who is responsable to perform the thoracentesis and then the procedure is scheduled.
Phase 2. Thoracentesis and pleural biopsy:

On the date scheduled, the medical team provides information about the procedure to the patient and he/she sign the informed consent. The patient is submitted to peripheral blood collection, which is stored in collection tubes, at the time of venous line insertion with conventional peripheral intravenous catheter and receives saline infision.
The patient sit on a bed or on the edge of a chair or bed with head and arms resting on a table. The skin around the procedure site is cleaned. The local anesthesia with lidocaine is performed.

Thoracentesis is performed by a physician trained for the procedure which is guided by chest ultrasound. During all the procedure the patient has its vital signs monitored and receives an infusion of saline solution in the venous line previously acquired. Aliquots of 50 milliliters of pleural fluid for conventional study are collected, stored in disposable jars and requested for: analysis of global and specific citometry, DHL, total proteins and albumin, cholesterol, triglycerides, glucose, total bilirubin and fractions, amylase, pH, acid fast bacilli smear microscopy, mycobacteria culture (on solid media), Xpert MTB/RIF®, culture for bacteria and fungus, cytopathology and adenosine deaminase dosage.

In cases where there are no contraindications to the procedure, it is decided to perform a pleural biopsy with a Cope needle, with 4 pleural fragments collected for histopathological study and for 2 pleural fragments collected to perform acid fast bacilli smear microscopy and culture for mycobacteria.
The biological specimens collected are send to the laboratory within one hour after the procedure.
Phase 3. Procedures after thoracentesis and pleural biopsy:

At the end of the procedure a chest X-ray is requested in order to evaluate possible imediate complications related to the procedure (pneumothorax, bleeding, bruising) and after exclusion of them, the patient is released to their home. In cases where complications are suspected the patient is hospitalized.
Phase 4. Follow up of the patients:

All patients return for medical examination two weeks after the procedure to receive the results of all exams requested. In cases of pleural tuberculosis diagnosis, the patients are referred for treatment and follow-up by the Tuberculosis Outpatient Clinic of HUPE / UERJ. Patients who have diagnoses other than tuberculosis are evaluated to be included in one of the various outpatient clinics of HUPE or are referred to their original service.
